headline: Congo DR's Persistence Breaks Uzbekistan's Spell
story: Uzbekistan stunned Congo DR with a miraculous 10th-minute opener—their expected goal of 0.01 suggested pure fortune. But Congo DR, operating in a 4-4-2, controlled what followed: 53 per cent possession, 19 shots, and the shape of a team that knew they would eventually overwhelm. The pressure mounted through the first hour, only to falter at the 61st minute when a glorious chance (0.25 xG) slipped past. Crucially, Congo DR didn't crack. Three goals in 23 minutes from the 68th minute onward sealed an emphatic recovery.

The numbers explain the chasm. Congo DR's expected goals of 2.11 against Uzbekistan's 0.16 reflected a suffocation: in their 4-4-2, Wissa (8.5), Elia (7.7), and Mayele (7.7) systematically dismantled a side unable to cope. Uzbekistan's ball-recovery time—13.6 seconds compared to Congo DR's brisk 10.4—meant constant dispossession under high-press phases (5.1 vs 4.3). Shomurodov (7.1) and company never gained purchase. The 68th and 78th-minute strikes came from Congo DR's superiority; the 90+1' finish, a low-xG affair (0.03), merely confirmed Uzbekistan's collapse.

keyMoment.text: Congo DR broke through in the 68th minute, converting their dominance into the lead after Uzbekistan's early fortune evaporated.

home.verdict: Possession, press, and patience won it; a missed 61st-minute chance nearly undid the script.
